rules.utility: Public Service Company of Colorado (Xcel Energy)
rules.threshold_text: 50 MW or more (mandatory for new loads over 50 MW per PSCo's 10-Q); new customers of 20 to 50 MW may also be subject to the tariff
rules.contract_term: 15 years or more (minimum initial term of 15 years)

rules.threshold_text: Over 20 MW aggregate at the same premises (special contract, Energy Services Agreement); new service requests of 1 MW or more are handled as large-load inquiries with engineering studies
rules.contract_term: No term printed; ESAs typically include notice and resizing limits
rules.collateral: No figure printed; ESAs typically include credit support requirements, and customer-specific delivery facilities are funded up front (CIAC)
rules.exit_fee: No figure printed; ESAs typically include termination and make-whole protections

rules.utility: Idaho Power Company (the statute binds every Idaho public utility, including Rocky Mountain Power and Avista in Idaho)
rules.threshold_text: An increase of 50 MW or more in a service entrance's cumulative power requirement in any consecutive 60-month period, under a service contract entered into on or after 1 July 2026; splitting load across service entrances does not change the status
rules.collateral: Financial security, in a form and amount approved by the commission, reasonably sufficient to protect the utility and its other customers from stranded or unrecoverable costs
rules.study_timeline: Commission review: the commission approves or denies a new large load service contract within 270 days of the utility's filing, which must include a no harm test; no engineering study clock

rules.utility: Nevada Power Company and Sierra Pacific Power Company (NV Energy)
rules.contract_term: total term not less than ten years after the Effective Date (Ramp Period plus the period after it; months left blank in the form); after long-term supply begins the customer may terminate on not less than 36 months' written notice
rules.collateral: ESA Customer Security within 15 Business Days after PUCN approval, equal to the aggregate Minimum Demand and Minimum Energy times the ESA Overall Rate for the remaining Term; letter of credit, cash deposit or affiliate guaranty; waived while the customer holds A- (S&P) and A3 (Moody's) ratings and liquidity above ten times the aggregate Minimum Demand times the ESA Overall Rate for the Term
rules.exit_fee: Termination Payment equal to the aggregate Minimum Demand times the ESA Overall Rate from the Termination Date to the end of the Term (excluding BTER, DEAA and other applicable rates), due within 30 days of the Termination Date; NV Energy mitigates it for 36 months after the Termination Date

rules.threshold_text: 20 MW: a facility primarily engaged in NAICS 518210 (data centers) that uses or is able to use 20 MW or more (Schedule 401 as filed: load registering 20,000 kW or greater, or Reserved Capacity of 20,000 kW or greater). Sites with common ownership within 2,500 feet of each other or served by the same substation count as one, and commonly owned data centers anywhere in the territory have their Contract Demand summed
rules.contract_term: Minimum 10 years, maximum 30 years, inclusive of any ramp period; renewals at least 10 years
rules.collateral: At the company's election, sufficient creditworthiness or posted collateral to cover the customer's Exit Fee; creditworthiness means senior unsecured long-term debt rated A- or higher (S&P or Fitch), A (low) or higher (DBRS) or A3 or higher (Moody's), or an equivalent internal rating; the amount is reassessed every two years. Network Upgrades needed for the load are paid up front by the LEUF, except Qualified Network Upgrades (230 kV and above, on the WECC critical path list, with less than 80 percent of known capacity needs from LEUFs), which are paid as a monthly fee on the LEUF's share
rules.exit_fee: Exit Fee set to recover company-funded infrastructure: net book value of company-funded infrastructure, net cost of customer-specific power or tolling agreements, the Reservation Charge for the remainder of the contract, and the net cost of removing facilities no longer needed; refunded pro rata if another large customer takes the capacity within three years (the removal cost is not refunded)
rules.study_timeline: No study deadline is set (the stipulating parties said a standard deadline is not possible). Company practice as testified: initial load interconnection system impact study in no more than six months after the required documents and study payment. LEUF Agreement filed within 45 days of execution; if none is executed within 180 days of completion of the service study, either party may file an unexecuted agreement; Commission review 90 days (standard agreement) or 180 days (non-conforming), extendable for good cause. Engineering studies are funded separately by the LEUF

rules.threshold_text: 50,000 kW of total Reserved Capacity (the Commission rejected the 25,000 kW proposed)
rules.contract_term: No minimum term printed in the sheets read; Reserved Capacity may be reduced by up to 10 percent of total load or 50 MW a year, whichever is smaller, or more by mutual agreement

rules.collateral: System capacity allocation deposit at contract signing equal to two years of minimum transmission demand, refunded 50 percent in year two and 50 percent in year three after energization if the customer meets 80 percent of its allocated system capacity and its contracted flexibility plan; uniform credit requirements in the tariff, including senior long-term debt rated A- (S&P) or A3 (Moody's); surety bonds accepted as collateral
rules.study_timeline: Study results expire after 60 days unless extended (Rule I, Section 2); no study duration printed

rules.threshold_text: 50,000 kVA of Reserved Capacity: new applicants signing after 25 April 2025 for total Reserved Capacity of 50,000 kVA or more, or existing customers adding 50,000 kVA above their 25 April 2025 Reserved Capacity. Customers requiring 200,000 kVA or more total load must take a special pricing contract
rules.contract_term: Minimum five years in addition to the specified load ramp period; Reserved Capacity may be reduced by up to 10 percent or 50,000 kVA a year, whichever is smaller, or more by mutual agreement
rules.collateral: Sufficient credit, or posted collateral at the Company's election, to cover the Minimum On-Peak Power Charge for at least five years

rules.utility: Public Utility District No. 1 of Snohomish County (Snohomish County PUD)
rules.threshold_text: aggregate anticipated demand greater than 2.5 MVA (net increase over a continuous five-year period); loads exceeding 10 MVA may need enhanced review and additional contractual terms; loads of 10 aMVA or more need a Power Supply Review
rules.collateral: formal credit evaluation; acceptable instruments include letters of credit, parental guarantees, performance security bonds or cash collateral, scaled to project maturity and risk; an up-front refundable deposit (refunded over ten years for customers who remain in service), which may be larger for loads over 10 aMVA
rules.exit_fee: on partial completion or demand shortfall, the District recovers all incurred expenses from the performance security; on nonpayment or abandonment, forfeiture of deposits, termination of service agreements or legal action; Demand Credits forfeited if energization is not reached by the end of the five-year Election Period
rules.study_timeline: policy: Feasibility Review approximately 2 weeks; System Impact Study approximately 1 to 4 months. PUD web page: application and feasibility review 1 to 2 months ($5,000); interconnection studies 3 to 8 months ($10,000 minimum); Power Supply Review typically two to three months, in parallel; final Power Service Agreement less than 1 month (the two documents differ; both are the PUD's)

rules.utility: Public Utility District No. 1 of Snohomish County (Snohomish County PUD)
rules.threshold_text: a load increase of ten average megawatts or more in any consecutive twelve months (a BPA New Large Single Load)
rules.collateral: no security terms printed; the PUD reserves the right to collect contributions in aid of construction or other charges for required capital expansion

rules.utility: Public Utility District No. 2 of Grant County (Grant PUD)
rules.threshold_text: A New Large Load is an increase of more than 10 average MW in a customer's annual average load above its highest annual average load since 2010; Large Power Customers start at 500 kW/kVA, and requests above 20 MVA need more detailed study
rules.collateral: No security amount printed; an up-front Customer Contribution under a Facilities Contribution Agreement, calculated to prevent shifting long-term costs to other rate classes (it does not reserve capacity); general deposit rules of Section 6.13 apply
rules.study_timeline: No study duration printed. A System Impact Study comes first; after the results consultation the customer has 30 calendar days to move into the Facilities Study or terminate the application

rules.utility: Seattle City Light (City of Seattle, City Light Department)
rules.threshold_text: 10 MVA or more of new or expanded data center capacity installed within any consecutive five-year period after 1 January 2027 (stated in MVA, not MW)
rules.contract_term: not exceeding 20 years (City Light's authority to sign data center contracts for new large loads)
rules.collateral: full upfront financial responsibility for the cost of any infrastructure needed to serve the customer; the contract may add other terms for security and financial risk (no amount stated)
rules.exit_fee: no exit fee is named; the customer stays fully responsible for the cost of the agreements City Light signed to serve its load until the contract term expires

queue_totals.utility: Public Utility District No. 2 of Grant County (Grant PUD)
queue_totals.figure: Approximately 800 MW of large-load requests in the power application queue (Grant PUD FAQ of 28 August 2026)

queue_totals.utility: Seattle City Light (City of Seattle, City Light Department)
queue_totals.figure: five proposed large data centers from four companies, combined maximum demand 369 MW (approaches to City Light reported in April 2026, as the City Council's release of 9 June 2026 states)

queue_totals.utility: Nevada Power Company and Sierra Pacific Power Company (NV Energy)
queue_totals.figure: about 22,000 MW (22 GW) of data center interest inquiries and about 6 GW of signed Rule 9 agreements; five customers proceeding toward eight LLESAs with aggregated load expected to exceed 3.3 GW by 2032 (application dated 6 May 2026)

Oregon: 20 interconnection requests from potential Schedule 401 customers, all above 100 MW, 7 above 250 MW and 3 above 500 MW (PacifiCorp data response of 3 April 2026, filed 11 June 2026); about 4 GW of potential added demand on the Oregon system at the most conservative estimate (company testimony, 11 June 2026). System-wide: over 5,000 MW of new large load requests across PacifiCorp's territory at various stages of study (same testimony)
